faqs.a:
(a)
Failure by owner to prevent disposition—Animal subject to a summons hold.
An animal subject to a summons hold which has not been claimed by its owner or custodian
               or whose owner or custodian has not been located within five days after its impoundment
               will be considered abandoned as of the sixth day after its impoundment and deemed
               by the court to be the property of the animal shelter. The shelter may then place
               the animal for adoption or otherwise dispose of the animal at the shelter's sole discretion.
(b)
Failure by owner to prevent disposition—Animal subject to a court hold.
An animal subject to a court hold whose owner or custodian does not file with the
               court either a payment or a petition as set forth in
section 14-204
(b) within ten days after its impoundment will be considered abandoned as of the eleventh
               day after its impoundment and deemed by the court to be the property of the animal
               shelter. The shelter may then place the animal for adoption or otherwise dispose of
               the animal at the shelter's sole discretion.
(c)
Owner liability.
(1)
Impoundment and shelter charges.
The failure of the owner or custodian of an impounded animal to prevent the disposition
               of the animal as set forth in
section 14-204
does not relieve the owner or custodian from payment of all applicable charges and
               fees established by the city for the impoundment of the animal or by the shelter for
               the care and provision of the animal. It shall be unlawful for an owner or custodian
               to fail to pay the costs of impoundment, care, and provision for the animal.
(2)
Criminal liability.
The failure of the owner or custodian of an impounded animal to prevent the disposition
               of the animal as set forth in
section 14-204
does not render the owner or custodian immune from service of a summons and complaint
               in the matter, from responsibility for a violation of the provisions of this chapter,
               or from decisions of the court relating to the matter, or for fees, fines, or other
               penalties which may result from a conviction for a violation of this chapter.
(3)
Release.
The failure of an owner to prevent the disposition of an animal as set forth in
section 14-204
releases the city and the animal shelter and their officers, employees, and agents
               from all liability for the animal's subsequent adoption, destruction, or other disposition.
(d)
Feral cats.
Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, a cat impounded and deemed to
               be feral by an animal management officer may be disposed of at the sole discretion
               of the animal shelter at any time three days after impoundment.
(e)
Emergency disposition.
(1)
Dangerous animals.
Nothing in this chapter may be construed to prevent the immediate destruction by
               an animal management officer of a dangerous animal when deemed necessary in the interest
               of public safety by that officer under circumstances where a significant and immediate
               threat to the health or safety of a person or another animal exists. Nothing in this
               chapter may be construed to prevent an officer from taking whatever action is reasonably
               necessary to protect themselves or others from injury or damage, including immediate
               destruction of a dangerous animal without notice to the owner or custodian. Moreover,
               nothing in this chapter may be construed to limit or restrict a person's ability to
               protect life and property under applicable Colorado law or to limit or restrict the
               authority of any employee or agent of the Colorado Division of Wildlife.
(2)
Ill or injured animals.
Nothing in this chapter may be construed to prevent the immediate destruction by
               an animal management officer or a veterinarian of any domestic or wild animal when
               the officer or veterinarian or has determined that such animal is critically ill or
               injured, is suffering extreme pain, or has a poor prognosis for recovery.
(f)
Process.
The city attorney may at any time after the time limits set forth in subsection (a)
               or (b) of this section file a motion seeking an order declaring an impounded animal
               to be abandoned, deeming the animal to be the property of the animal shelter, and
               authorizing the shelter to take any action it deems necessary to provide for the disposition
               of the animal.
(
Ord. No. 4878
, § 9, 10-7-2024)
